Chrono.notes:
The HEADS legend is wrong. Chrono.cpp:198-205 holds six head-level rows, each giving the triplet, beat and dotted heads a weight of 1 or 0.5, and the maker's own comments name them ALL, TRP, DOT, QTR, DUB, SUB from row 0 upward — the reverse of the configSwitch labels at Chrono.cpp:215, which are SUB, DUB, QTR, DOT, TRP, ALL from value 0. The slider's minimum is at the bottom (Chrono.cpp:52-55), so value 0 is the SUB position, and it applies the all-equal row. Matched against the lit squares drawn on Chrono.svg the table does not line up in either direction: the panel's DOT pattern, outer two heads loud and the middle one quiet, does not exist in the table at all. What the six positions actually do, from SUB upward: all three heads full; triplet full; beat full; dotted full; triplet and beat full; beat and dotted full, with the remaining heads at half level in each case.

The manual calls the second momentary button Break and describes a tape-stop slowdown. The panel prints DRY, the parameter is named Dry, and the code crossfades to the dry input over 1 second (Chrono.cpp:327-335, 687-688). The tape-stop machinery is still in the file — brakeSpeed and brakeSpeedSmooth at Chrono.cpp:153-154 — but nothing ever writes to them, so brakeSpeedSmooth stays at 1 and the slowdown never happens.

The manual lists stereo audio inputs. Only IN/L is written into the delay buffer (Chrono.cpp:439, 525); IN/R reaches the output through the dry path alone (Chrono.cpp:675), so the echoes are mono however the module is patched.

There is no tone control: the variable named tone is fixed at 1.0 at Chrono.cpp:290.

Orbit.notes:
A fifth output, Rhythmic distance CV, is configured at Orbit.cpp:87 and is written every sample at Orbit.cpp:473, but the widget deliberately adds no jack for it; the maker's comment at Orbit.cpp:541-542 says it is kept for old beta patches and is redundant with Tension. The manual does not say which way the tension voltage runs. liveTensionVoltage at Orbit.cpp:131 returns ten times one minus the distance, so the voltage is highest when the two rhythms land together and falls to zero when they are a full Range apart.

Alignment output is thinned: a pair of edges within a hundredth of the reference period is treated as an exact alignment and fires only on every second occurrence, and no two align pulses are allowed closer than a sixteenth of the reference period (Orbit.cpp:362-375).

Window does two jobs. It sets the alignment window as an eighth of a beat plus the square root of the knob times seven eighths (Orbit.cpp:357-359), and it sets the gap delay as half a beat minus three eighths of the knob (Orbit.cpp:439-441), so raising it widens alignment and shortens the wait for a gap.

With no clock patched, the reference period falls back to the average of the two measured rhythm periods, or to half a second if neither has been measured (Orbit.cpp:289-295).

Circles.notes:
Two things on this module cannot be reached. An End of cycle output is configured at Circles.cpp:297 and written every sample at Circles.cpp:939, pulsing 1ms whenever the sequence returns to step 1, but no jack is added for it. A Scale chain length parameter is configured at Circles.cpp:255 and is still read at Circles.cpp:318, but only to convert older patches the first time they are opened (Circles.cpp:342-349); the four Include buttons replaced it and no widget exists for it. The Gate knob is used twice, against different lengths: for the main gate it is a fraction of one step, and for the sub gate a fraction of one bar (Circles.cpp:310-315, 809-813), so the same setting gives a much longer sub gate.

Selecting a different scale slot with the sub track's SCALE control writes the stored step back into the STEP parameter (Circles.cpp:517-520), so that knob moves on its own when SCALE is turned.

The eight step knobs, their enable buttons and the step CV jacks are all real ParamWidgets and PortWidgets, so each can be clicked; the central display is one custom widget and cannot.
